description: A tool a workflow installs with `go install module@vN` is a pinned dependency that no manager reads. Renovate's gomod manager looks at go.mod; github-actions looks at `uses:`; a version inside a `run:` block is seen by neither, so it is a pin that will never be offered an update.

Measured on 2026-10-11, the day it bit: both repositories in this organisation pin `github.com/go-fleettools/fleettools/cmd/vulngate@v0.7.0` in their known-vulnerabilities lane, and the module reached v0.8.0 the same afternoon. Six hours. `github.com/rhysd/actionlint/cmd/actionlint@v1.7.12` is pinned the same way in both and happens to be current, which is luck rather than a mechanism. The gate that judges vulnerability findings going quietly stale is the worst of the three places this could happen.

depName is the MODULE, not the package: `go install` takes a package path, and the proxy knows modules. ⛔ This used to say every tool in this fleet lives at `<module>/cmd/<name>`, which is FALSE and argues for making the group mandatory: go-fleettools/prwait and go-fleettools/staletools have their main package at the module ROOT. The group is optional for exactly that reason, and both shapes were measured against this rule on 2026-10-18 — `…/cmd/vulngate@v0.20.1` gives `fleettools`, `…/prwait@v0.2.1` gives `prwait`, and `govulncheck@latest` is correctly unmatched. A module whose own path ends in `/cmd/<something>` would still be read wrong; none does here.

A version of `latest` is deliberately NOT matched: there is no version to compare or rewrite. That is the same hole `gopin` was written for, where `go-version: stable` in a workflow had Renovate doing nothing for seven repositories while CI quietly moved a minor. `govulncheck@latest` in these lanes is a deliberate float, not an oversight.

One pull request per repository for everything non-breaking, rather than one per dependency. Merging them singly means every merge rebases the others and restarts their checks: one run over an organisation of 34 repositories updated 109 branches and merged 2. Grouped, a repository needs one round of checks instead of dozens.

Never auto-merge the Go toolchain, and never let it ride in somebody else's group. A rule that says automerge:false for one dependency is defeated by grouping, because Renovate decides automerge per BRANCH: go 1.27.0 rode into seven repositories inside a branch called renovate/github-actions, whose other dependency was actions/setup-go. Ungrouped, it gets a branch of its own and this setting governs it. It matters because go1.27.0 miscompiles on loong64 (golang/go#81000, bisected on real hardware to 3fdac6780b): go-gfx/gfx fails that lane and stayed open only because the lane failed, which is the CI gate holding rather than this rule. A repository without such a lane sees nothing.
